title: Animation and window size
cards/0/body: renderer.render draws a single frame. To make things move, you have to keep drawing frames, about 60 times a second, and change the scene in between.
cards/1/task: The cube is standing still. Make it spin.
cards/2/q: Why is setAnimationLoop better than your own while(true) loop?
cards/2/options/0: The browser calls your function before each screen frame and the page does not freeze
cards/2/explain: Under the hood it uses requestAnimationFrame, and you also need it for VR/AR sessions.
cards/3/title: Speed should not depend on the monitor
cards/3/body: With += 0.01 per frame, the cube spins more than twice as fast on a 144 Hz monitor as on a 60 Hz one. The right way is to multiply by the time since the last frame.
cards/4/q: On a teammate's 120 Hz monitor the cube spins twice as fast. Why?
cards/4/options/0: Rotation is added per frame, not per second, and they get twice as many frames
cards/4/explain: Multiply the speed by dt from THREE.Clock.
cards/5/body: When the window size changes, update both the camera and the renderer. Otherwise the picture gets stretched.
cards/6/q: The window got wider and the cube looks squashed. Tap the line that should be followed by one more call.
cards/6/explain: After changing aspect (or fov, near, far) you need camera.updateProjectionMatrix(). Otherwise the camera keeps using the old values.
cards/7/options/0: On a screen with pixel ratio 3 you would render 9 times as many pixels, which is heavy for a phone
cards/7/options/1: It does not work without it
cards/7/explain: A ratio of 2 already looks sharp, and the cost grows with the square.
